qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Putative distribution scale and broad ANDA regulatory approval portfolio fail to confer pricing power or excess economic returns. Generics face intense structural price erosion (3-5%+ annually) from consolidated wholesale buying consortia (McKesson, Cencora, Cardinal Health) and low-cost global manufacturers. 10-year median ROIC of 6.5% tracks below cost of capital, deteriorating to flat/negative in FY24-25.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC 6.5% < 12% hurdle, negative pricing power, REJECT). Generic and off-patent pharmaceutical manufacturing is a structural commodity price-taker business facing persistent 3-5%+ annual price erosion driven by consolidated wholesale buying consortia (McKesson, Cencora, Cardinal Health). 10-year median ROIC of 6.5% fails the 12% hurdle and tracks below WACC, with 2024-2025 ROIC depressed to flat/negative. Capital allocation has focused on divestitures (biosimilars, OTC, API) to service legacy Mylan/Upjohn debt rather than compounding per-share intrinsic value.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 6.5% (v1 financial data; FY24 ROIC ~0.02%, FY25 ROIC negative at -5.58% amid restructuring charges and facility remediations, TTM ROIC ~2.7-4.4% vs WACC of ~6.6-7.3%). Annual generic pricing erosion of 3-5% acts as a permanent top-line drag on base business. Formed from November 2020 merger of Mylan and Pfizer's Upjohn division with ~$25B in initial debt; subsequent divestitures (biosimilars to Biocon for $3.3B, OTC/API prunings) generated cash for debt reduction (lowering debt toward ~$16-17B with ~$2B annual FCF), but organic revenue growth remains constrained by commodity tender pricing and generic commoditization.
